RagShortTexts: In 1259 Henry III and Louis IX negotiated continental rights; news traveled unevenly.

Variants.Content: Different regions faced distinct struggles for power in 1259. Mongol campaigns and news of Baghdad’s sack in 1258 shook the Islamic world. Henry III and Louis IX negotiated continental rights including Aquitaine, while the English crown and barons disputed government. Nicaea sought Constantinople, and Iberian rulers managed southern territories and local communities. Envoys, ships and merchants carried news unevenly between courts and villages.
